repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until((#Garden_Button).button_button != "pushed")
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Garden_Button).button_button == "pushed")
(#Garden_Valve).valve_open()
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a repeating rising-edge wait that must block until the button transitions to 'pushed' and then fire. The candidate uses a periodic `if` which only checks the condition at the start of the 1-second wrapper. Since the button was already 'pushed' at t=100ms (the first check point), the candidate evaluated the `if`, found the condition true, but failed to emit the action because the logic inside the `if` was not structured as a blocking wait followed by a call. The IR requires blocking on the edge, not sampling it.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with the standard rising-edge state machine pattern: initialize a `fired` flag, block until the condition becomes false (to re-arm), block until the condition becomes true (the rising edge), then execute the body. This ensures the action fires exactly when the rising edge is detected and handles re-arming correctly for subsequent cycles.
